original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Audit the literal connector-covering-code Engine::search branching, sibling isolation, witness and interruption contract against independently enumerated Cartesian-domain ordinary words. Close PR3261's named search-completeness handoff, not a full B census.
scope_change_reason: PR2973's parity counterexample and corrected exclusion are already independently covered. PR3261 explicitly leaves branching/exhaustion validation open after capacity, propagation and representation audits. This audit checks that distinct remaining implication in the successor engine.
bottleneck_link: A finite exclusion needs both sound pruning and complete traversal. This closes the branch/backtrack implication without treating local checks as a complete seven-source or multiplication theorem.
stop_rule: Stop after one source-pinned search implication and bounded Cartesian/control replay. No full A/B exhaustion, new singleton search, native supplier or selected-frontier change.
evidence: README.md proof; RESULT.json fixes 914 roots, 3785826 direct tuples, 50 branching satisfiable and 22 branching unsatisfiable roots, four compiled semantic mutants, three interruption controls and two enumeration-return controls. CHECKS.json records actual execution and limits.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Substantial automated assistance in derivation, implementation, verification and writing. No independent human or proof-kernel review claimed.

overlap.coverage_limit: Metadata, live handoff, local source and peer reservations, not arbitrary diffs or unpublished work. No pending Git object is required by replay. Discussion drafts stay local under the supplied communication restriction.

open_questions.question: Does the complete cycle replay bind all 82 A/B templates and flags to genuinely completed source-pinned exhaustion?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Complete local traversal is not complete coverage of the caller's requested exclusion domain.
open_questions.first_step: Audit the replay caller's receipt acceptance, template inventory and interrupted-status handling, then separately budget an independent full B exhaustion.
open_questions.blocked_by: This audit neither executes the full B census nor checks the external literature/classification premises or non-simple branch.
